about.title: South El Monte Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: South El Monte is a compact Los Angeles County city of just under 21,000 people, and products are part of every hour of life here: a power tool at a job on Rush Street, a space heater in a home near Durfee Avenue, a tire or brake component on a car heading down Garvey Avenue or Santa Anita Avenue. Nearly all of them work as intended. When one does not, and a person is injured, California law treats the situation differently from an ordinary accident. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to show the company was careless. The questions are whether the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and whether that defect caused your harm. The manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer who sold it may each share responsibility. One practical step matters right away: keep the product, its packaging, and any receipts, and do not try to repair it. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match South El Monte residents with an independent attorney who takes product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Strict Liability Explained Plainly
items.desc: Product cases in California usually turn on whether the item was defective and caused your injury, not on proving the maker was negligent. The attorney you are connected with can walk you through which defect theory fits your situation.

items.title: Help Preserving the Evidence
items.desc: The product itself is often the heart of the case. An attorney can guide you on storing it safely, documenting its condition, and requesting records before anything is lost or discarded.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Considered
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be liable under California law. An independent attorney reviews the full path the product took to reach you so no responsible party is overlooked.

items.question: A part on my car failed during a crash on Garvey Avenue in South El Monte. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. South El Monte recorded 93 injury collisions in 2025, and in some of those, a defective airbag, seatbelt, tire, or brake component contributes to the harm even when another driver is also at fault. An attorney can evaluate whether the vehicle or part had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect alongside any claim against the other driver. Keeping the vehicle unrepaired until it is inspected is important.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was dangerous?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the manufacturer was careless or knew about the problem. This is one of the ways product cases differ from many other personal injury claims. An attorney can explain how these rules apply to your specific facts.

items.question: I bought the product at a local store, not from the manufacturer. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Under California law, the retailer that sold you the product, the distributor that supplied it, and the manufacturer that made it may all be held liable. You do not have to pick one before you talk with an attorney. Save your receipt, packaging, and the product itself, and let the attorney sort out which parties belong in the claim.
